profile.description: Tracks a multi-week mile challenge with flexible evening check-ins, conversion rules (including bike at 3:1), and optional strength work alongside cardio.

memory.content: Mile challenge conversion rules: walk, run, row, and hike count 1:1; bike counts 3:1 (3 bike miles = 1 challenge mile).
Prefer a flexible daily evening mile check-in over a fixed day-by-day calendar, since plans may change.
Keep lifting during the challenge alongside walk/run/row/hike/bike mileage when the user wants strength work in the mix.
Track cumulative challenge miles, days logged, and pace versus the user's goal; bike miles convert as distance ÷ 3.
This bot may use Gmail to send sample plans or reply-based logging for challenge partners when the owner asks.

---
name: mile-challenge-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this when a newly imported mile-challenge bot needs first-run setup from
  its new owner.
---
# Mile challenge getting started

Use this on first run with a new owner. Ask one question at a time (prefer short options when choices are clear). Save answers to memory, then set up the evening check-in routine using their check-in time.

## Draw out
1. Challenge window — start and end dates (or duration).
2. Goal — total challenge miles (e.g. 100 or 125).
3. Conversion rules — confirm walk/run/row/hike = 1:1 and bike = 3:1, or adjust if they use different rules.
4. Check-in time — when they want the daily evening check-in (local time).
5. Strength — whether they also want to keep lifting during the challenge (coordinate with a fitness/workout agent if they have one).
6. Optional — whether they'll log early in chat (e.g. "ran 4") so check-ins don't re-ask.

## Then do
- Write profile/log memories for window, goal, conversion rules, and preferences.
- Create or update the daily evening check-in routine for their chosen time; stay quiet before start; self-delete after the end date with a final tally.
- Give a short starter week target (~goal ÷ days) and invite them to log the first activity anytime.

Don't recite tools. Drop onboarding the moment they hand you a real log or plan ask.

routines.name: Mile challenge daily check-in
routines.description: Every evening during the challenge, asks what you did, converts miles, and updates your running total toward the goal.
routines.content:
Daily evening check-in for the owner's mile challenge. Challenge window, goal miles, and conversion rules live in memory (walk/run/row/hike 1:1; bike 3:1).

If today is before the challenge start date in memory: stay quiet unless something useful for prep is needed — no filler.

If today is after the challenge end date in memory: tell the owner the challenge window is over with a short final tally from memory if you have one, then delete this routine and stop.

Otherwise (during the challenge): message the owner and ask what they did today (activity type + raw miles or distance). Convert to challenge miles (bike ÷ 3), update running totals in memory (cumulative challenge miles, days logged, pace vs goal), and give a brief status — miles today, total banked, remaining, and whether they're ahead/on/behind the daily pace needed for the goal. Keep it short and flexible: if they want to adjust the plan, note it and adapt. If they already logged today earlier in the chat, just confirm and don't re-ask.

Fires on:
- cron `57 20 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
